practical_scenarios.title: SME disputes the user-tested wording
practical_scenarios.situation: A subject-matter expert insists on internal terminology even though user testing shows that readers do not understand it.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Acknowledge the domain concern, separate technical precision from surface vocabulary, show the test evidence, propose a defined term or dual-language pattern, and agree a decision owner and validation criterion.

practical_scenarios.title: Critical procedure is wrong before release
practical_scenarios.situation: A release candidate changes a command and the published setup procedure will fail when the product launches in four hours.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Confirm the behavior with an authoritative source, stop or correct the affected publication, coordinate with release and support, add a targeted validation, communicate scope, and record the process failure for prevention.

practical_scenarios.title: No time for documentation
practical_scenarios.situation: A product manager says the feature must ship and documentation can follow later.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Assess user and operational risk, define the minimum viable content and support readiness required for launch, show consequences and dependencies, negotiate scope or release conditions, and document the accepted risk.

practical_scenarios.title: Generated API reference is unusable
practical_scenarios.situation: The API portal contains complete generated endpoints but developers cannot complete an end-to-end workflow.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Keep generated reference as the contract view, analyze priority developer journeys, add authentication, quickstart, workflow, errors and examples, validate with fresh users, and connect feedback to the specification.
evaluation_criteria: Improves both portal and source contract

practical_scenarios.title: Documentation build passes but example fails
practical_scenarios.situation: All CI checks are green, but a customer reports that a code sample no longer compiles.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Reproduce against the documented version, correct or roll back the example, add executable tests and dependency controls, review similar samples, and explain that build success did not validate runtime behavior.

practical_scenarios.title: Accessibility defect discovered late
practical_scenarios.situation: A keyboard-only reviewer cannot navigate the documentation tabs one day before launch.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Treat it as a product-blocking content interaction defect based on impact, provide an accessible fallback or fix, test with keyboard and assistive technology, document the component issue, and add it to design-system validation.

practical_scenarios.title: Translation contains unsafe instruction
practical_scenarios.situation: A localized procedure reverses a condition and tells users to delete the wrong resource.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Pause the affected locale, verify source and translation, issue a corrected version and support alert, investigate terminology and QA failure, update translation memory carefully, and test other locales sharing the segment.

practical_scenarios.title: Knowledge base search returns obsolete pages
practical_scenarios.situation: Users repeatedly open an old workaround above the current resolution.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Remove or redirect obsolete content, fix status and ranking signals, preserve required history outside the default journey, analyze queries and links, and establish event-driven review for the affected product.

practical_scenarios.title: Support team creates duplicate articles
practical_scenarios.situation: Analysts create a new article for each case because search is slow and article improvement requires approval.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Measure the workflow friction, improve search and article structure, allow qualified users to edit within governance, coach search-first behavior, merge duplicates and track reuse and findability instead of article count.

practical_scenarios.title: Executive asks for page-view success metric
practical_scenarios.situation: A leader wants the documentation team judged only by total page views.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Clarify the decision the metric should support, explain ambiguous interpretations, propose a balanced set including task success, failed search, support impact, quality and maintenance, and report page views as context rather than value alone.

practical_scenarios.title: Content owner has left the company
practical_scenarios.situation: A high-risk operational runbook has no active owner after a reorganization.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Assign temporary accountable ownership, verify current technical behavior with operations, restrict or label unverified content if needed, map dependencies, and update the governance process to detect ownership changes.

practical_scenarios.title: CMS migration deadline requires moving everything
practical_scenarios.situation: Leadership wants all legacy content migrated before the contract ends, including pages with no usage or owner.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Separate preservation from publication, inventory and risk-classify assets, migrate only justified current content into the live experience, archive records appropriately, automate redirects and document exceptions and rollback.

practical_scenarios.title: Engineer rejects editorial review
practical_scenarios.situation: An engineer says grammar does not matter because the commands are technically correct.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Agree that technical correctness is essential, then demonstrate how ambiguity, structure and terminology affect safe execution, focus review on user risk and task outcomes, and keep stylistic rules proportionate.

practical_scenarios.title: AI assistant invents a configuration option
practical_scenarios.situation: A polished AI-generated draft includes a plausible option that does not exist.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Stop publication, verify every technical claim against authorized sources, identify whether restricted data was exposed, correct the draft, add provenance and structured review controls, and test the workflow for similar hallucinations.

practical_scenarios.situation: Security proposes removing public troubleshooting because some commands reveal system details.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Perform a threat and audience analysis, separate public safe diagnostics from restricted operational procedures, remove secrets and unsafe bypasses, document least-privilege examples, and agree review and escalation rules.

practical_scenarios.title: Two sources of truth conflict
practical_scenarios.situation: The product documentation and support knowledge base give different recovery instructions.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Contain the risk by identifying the authoritative current behavior, correct and cross-link both channels, define ownership by content purpose, remove duplicated canonical instructions where possible, and add synchronization triggers.

practical_scenarios.title: Community content is popular but inaccurate
practical_scenarios.situation: A highly viewed community article solves many cases but contains an unsafe shortcut.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Preserve the useful user language, correct or clearly moderate the unsafe step, publish an authoritative alternative, contact the contributor where possible, and improve search and feedback paths so trusted content is easier to find.

practical_scenarios.title: Documentation program loses funding
practical_scenarios.situation: Leadership views documentation as a cost center and plans to cut maintenance capacity.
practical_scenarios.preferred_response: Present a portfolio view of user tasks, incidents, support demand, release dependencies and risk, identify the minimum sustainable service, propose targeted experiments, and make the consequences of deferred maintenance explicit.
